name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a one-time theme picker at first launch, defaulting to the system preference but letting users override it once. This balances speed and preference: users see what they expect by default, but those who deviate—like a light-theme developer on a dark OS—aren’t stuck fighting the system. The trade-off is a small upfront friction for a one-time choice, but it avoids perpetual toggling and keeps the interface both familiar and flexible.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A one-time picker forces users to make a decision they may not care about—most will just click through, leaving them stuck with the system default anyway. The real risk is over-engineering a "solution" that solves no real problem while adding complexity. Ship the system default, then let users toggle *later* if glare or preference demands it—no picker, no friction, no false promises.
